prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1391; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at impact. Scene photos and the other driver's statement match the account given in the initial report.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection shows damage consistent with the described impact and speed. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files or in the prior-claims database.

Entry 5: Medical records show a neck strain, which fits the type and force of this collision. No prior injury to the cervical area is known from the claimant's history or from available records.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has been consistent across the recorded statement, the attorney's written demand, and the follow-up call. Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 7: Reviewed the file with the handling supervisor. Facts support the reported injury and the accident as described, and the claim is proceeding to evaluation under the standard represented-claimant process.
